k-mer-tokenization.name: k-mer tokenization
k-mer-tokenization.def: Splitting DNA into fixed-length tokens of k nucleotides. Nucleotide Transformer uses six-nucleotide k-mers; such tokens can split regulatory motifs and hide the effect of a single-nucleotide variant.

learned-variable-length-tokens.name: Learned variable-length tokens
learned-variable-length-tokens.def: Multinucleotide tokens whose lengths are learned from genomic sequences rather than fixed in advance (DNABERT-2, GROVER). Like k-mers, they can split motifs and hide single-nucleotide variants.

single-nucleotide-tokenization.name: Single-nucleotide tokenization
single-nucleotide-tokenization.def: Keeping one nucleotide per token to retain single-nucleotide resolution over long distances; it requires architectures that remain efficient over long inputs.

expression-rank-encoding.name: Expression-rank encoding
expression-rank-encoding.def: Representing a cell as genes ordered by expression rank, so that expression is encoded only by position in the input and not by its quantitative value; this sidesteps platform- and processing-specific confounders.

binned-expression-encoding.name: Binned expression-value encoding
binned-expression-encoding.def: Pairing each gene with a binned expression value, so that expression magnitude is represented explicitly.

genes-as-protein-embeddings.name: Genes represented by protein embeddings
genes-as-protein-embeddings.def: Representing each gene by the ESM2 embedding of its protein rather than by a fixed gene list, so that cells from species absent from training can be placed in a shared space.

structure-function-tokens.name: Structure and function tokens
structure-function-tokens.def: Adding tokens for local structure or function alongside amino acids: SaProt pairs each amino acid with a local-structure token, and ESM3 can be prompted with structure and function tokens.

prior-knowledge-tokens.name: Prior-knowledge-enriched tokens
prior-knowledge-tokens.def: Enriching gene tokens with prior knowledge before training.

sequence-clustering.name: Sequence clustering before training
sequence-clustering.def: Clustering protein databases by sequence similarity before training, because many sequences are near-duplicates of close evolutionary relatives.

alignment-augmented-input.name: Alignment-augmented input
alignment-augmented-input.def: Adding aligned sequences of related genomes or proteins as input, which makes conservation visible. GPN-MSA adds alignments from 100 vertebrate genomes; AlphaFold also uses alignments of related sequences.

long-context-architectures.name: Long-context architectures
long-context-architectures.def: Architectures designed to stay efficient over very long inputs; HyenaDNA reaches one million nucleotides.

likelihood-scoring-of-variants.name: Likelihood scoring of variants
likelihood-scoring-of-variants.def: Scoring how plausible a sequence is given the sequences a model was trained on; a mutation that makes the sequence much less plausible is more likely to disrupt function.

prompting-partial-structure-function.name: Prompting with partial structure or function
prompting-partial-structure-function.def: Generating a sequence by giving the model a partial specification of structure or function as a prompt (ESM3).

similarity-aware-splitting.name: Similarity-aware train/test splitting
similarity-aware-splitting.def: Removing from the test set sequences that have close relatives in the training set, so that a high score reflects learned rules and not recall.

calibrated-metrics.name: Calibrated metrics (mean baseline + positive control)
calibrated-metrics.def: Calibrating a metric against both an uninformative mean baseline and a positive control. Under such metrics several deep-learning perturbation models do outperform simple baselines.

shuffled-input-control.name: Shuffled-input control
shuffled-input-control.def: Replacing biological inputs with shuffled ones to test whether the encoder contributes to a system's accuracy. BioReason and BioReason-Pro were as accurate with shuffled inputs as with intact ones.

packaging-as-mcp-tool.name: Packaging a model as an MCP tool
packaging-as-mcp-tool.def: Wrapping a database, program, or FM once as an MCP tool so that any compatible agent can use it. Paper2Agent turns a paper's codebase into MCP tools.
